title: Fast-Follow Microtranches: Experiment to Reserve Capacity for Unplanned High-Priority Work
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a two-week pilot that allocates a small dedicated microtranche (target 8% of total engineering capacity, range 5-12%) as a fast-follow reserve to absorb unplanned high-priority work (customer incidents, urgent compliance requests, hotfixes for revenue-impacting regressions). The goal is to validate whether a bounded reserved lane reduces disruption to committed initiatives while keeping time-to-response for urgent issues under SLAs. Deliverables: playbook for microtranche sizing, staffing rotation pattern, monitoring dashboard, and a recommendation for incorporation into cycle planning templates.
acceptance_criteria: Microtranche is formally reserved in sprint planning for the two-week pilot and visible on the cycle board
No more than 1 planned P1 deliverable is delayed by >3 business days due to absorbed work during the pilot
Mean time to acknowledge and begin remediation for prioritized unplanned requests falls below 4 hours
Quantitative disruption index (see playbook) shows >=40% reduction in cross-team context-switching vs baseline week
Pilot playbook (sizing, gating signals, rotation, escalation) is reviewed and approved by Eng + Product leadership
steps: Finalize microtranche definition and sizing band (target 8%, floor 5%, cap 12%)
Agree gating signals for when work is eligible for the fast-follow lane (severity, revenue impact, compliance/legal)
Coordinate with Eng leads to assign 1-2 rotating responders per squad and define shadow/backup rules
Add microtranche swimlane to cycle board and update planning checklist templates
Run a 3-day tabletop simulation to validate handoffs and tooling (on-call -> microtranche -> escalation)
Enable lightweight dashboard (tickets routed, hours consumed, lost planned points) and instrument disruption index
Execute two-week pilot, capture metrics and qualitative notes, hold retro and finalize recommendation
decisions: Allocation: start at 8% of engineering capacity; allow auto-burst to 12% if no >2 open planned blockers remain

Gating: work enters fast-follow lane if it meets ANY of: (a) customer-reported outage with >1% revenue exposure, (b) regulatory/compliance deadline within 7 days, (c) security incident triaged to severity S2+
Staffing: rotating 2-person coverage per squad on a 1-week shadow cadence; rotation schedule maintained in shared calendar
Fallback: if microtranche is saturated and new eligible work arrives, triage with PM rotation and defer non-critical planned tasks as temporary backfill
Measurement: use a disruption index combining task switches, percentage of planned points paused, and average rework time; target >=40% improvement
